assumptions: W7 of PLAN-0006: Confluence requirements-template intake, built in-session by a single writer, added to .warp/tracker_intake.py (the same module as the WARP-0604 Jira intake - the same feature, reusing resolve_repo, _fm_safe, render_spec_markdown, and the seam; no parallel machinery per C3). A structured requirements page becomes a routing-resolved spec draft whose acceptance criteria come FROM the page (a feature, not a reproduction). The intake LOGIC (parse_requirements, draft_spec_from_requirements) and the page MAPPING (_confluence_page_to_item, _confluence_text XHTML flatten) are mechanical and gate-tested over the FakeTracker + a fixture page; the live ConfluenceCloudAdapter is reference-wired (needs live Confluence, not gate-run, token from a secrets ref). A requirements-page template ships at plugin/templates/confluence-requirements-template.md. No template twin (not a validate/policy_check load dependency). A REVIEW-DRIVEN robustness fix was applied to the reviewed code and re-reviewed: _confluence_page_to_item now guards a None page at the top (page = page or {}) for full consistency with the body guard, so a None page yields a benign item instead of raising (non-exploitable in the real flow but a half-guard is fixed), covered by a new selftest assertion. Two independent adversarial reviews (the full pass on 5ecd808 and a scoped re-review bound to this commit 09200df) both PASS with 0 blocking; the full review could not break routing, the parse/mapping, the secrets fail-closed, the injection guard, or produce an invalid draft.

The requirement's ACs come from the page's Acceptance Criteria section (renumbered AC1..ACn) with a no-regression ACn appended; a page with no AC section falls back to a single capture AC + no-regression. The routing signal is a page label (the same mechanism as Jira), so no new routing path. Untrusted page content is sanitized by the same _fm_safe guard, so page text is a scalar value never a structural key; a body-embedded second front-matter block is ignored by the validator's first-block match.
